summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727KB payload
details: Package published under the @hubsync scope but branded as 'Verdocs Web SDK for React' (dist references api.verdocs.com/beta.verdocs.com), an identity mismatch not present in the legitimate upstream. package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs` that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (or uses `bun` if already on PATH) and invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled 727KB `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a single-line obfuscated bundle (rotating string/number dictionary `n7gIxM`, `WV8StW` array-rotate, `_bun-cjs` header) whose behavior is not visible as plain literals; setup.mjs itself uses obfuscator.io-style `_0x...` identifiers. Fetching an alternate language runtime purely to execute an opaque bundled script at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern — a React SDK has no legitimate need to shell out to Bun, and the Bun-executed branch bypasses Node-based scanners. The payload runs automatically on `npm install` with the installer's user privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
